Privacy Policy

Ponlet Privacy Policy

Last Updated: September 8, 2026
Platforms: Android (jp.yasagure.ponlet), Web, iOS, Desktop

Zero Data Retention Policy

Connections are established directly via peer-to-peer (WireGuard / WebRTC DataChannel) whenever possible. In environments where NAT traversal or firewall restrictions make direct connection difficult, packets are relayed through DERP relay servers. Even when passing through relays, all communications remain end-to-end encrypted (E2EE) with WireGuard, making it technically impossible for the server to inspect or store any transferred content (file data or text), ensuring Zero Data Retention.

01

Overview & Zero Data Retention

Core Principles

This Privacy Policy outlines how Ponlet ("the App") handles data. The App encompasses the Android client (package name: jp.yasagure.ponlet), the Web client, iOS client, and desktop versions (macOS/Windows/Linux).

The App is architected with privacy by design as its foundational principle. We do not operate centralized file storage servers, and we enforce a strict Zero Data Retention policy—neither developers nor servers ever collect, view, or retain your transferred data or personal information.

Never Collected
Accounts & Identity

No user account or login is ever required. We never collect or request names, email addresses, phone numbers, or passwords.

Never Stored
Files & Messages

Transferred photos, documents, and clipboard text exist only on participating peer devices and are never stored on any server.

Opt-Out Telemetry
Telemetry (Usage Reporting)

Limited telemetry for quality improvement is provided on an opt-out basis (enabled by default; it can be turned off from the footer at the bottom of the app). No advertising SDKs are included, and transferred content such as file names or message text is never sent. See "4. Telemetry" for details.

02

Communication Architecture & DERP Relays

P2P & Encrypted Relay

Communications are established directly between devices via peer-to-peer (WireGuard / WebRTC DataChannel) whenever possible. In restrictive environments—such as symmetric NAT or strict corporate firewalls—packets are relayed through public DERP (Designated Encrypted Relay for Packets) relay servers.

  • End-to-End Encryption (E2EE): All packets are encrypted end-to-end between peer devices using the WireGuard protocol. DERP relay servers merely route opaque, encrypted packets without possessing decryption keys. It is cryptographically impossible for relays to inspect or modify the content of your transmissions.
  • Volatile In-Memory Processing: Transient network metadata (SDP, ICE candidates) used during peer discovery is handled purely in volatile memory and discarded immediately upon session establishment or disconnection. No data is written to disk or recorded in access logs.
  • Confidential Invite Links: The 32-byte shared cryptographic key is embedded exclusively in the URL hash fragment (#i=...). Under the HTTP standard, hash fragments are handled entirely by the browser client and are never sent across the network to hosting servers (such as Cloudflare Pages) or logged in server logs.
03

Local Data Storage

Device-Level Management

All received files and messages are strictly stored and managed locally on your own devices:

Web Client
Volatile Browser Memory

Transferred files are temporarily held in browser memory (Blob) and written to your Downloads folder only when you choose to save them. Closing the browser tab immediately purges the memory.

Native Apps
Local Storage Directory

On Android, iOS, and desktop platforms, files are saved directly into your authorized local folders (e.g., standard Downloads). The app never uploads local files without explicit instruction.

04

Telemetry (Usage Reporting)

Opt-Out Telemetry

The App includes opt-out telemetry (usage reporting) for the purpose of quality improvement and stability. Telemetry is enabled by default and can be turned off at any time using the "Send telemetry" toggle in the footer at the bottom of the app.

  • Google Analytics for Firebase (Analytics): Used on iOS / Android / Web.
  • Firebase Crashlytics: Used on iOS / Android. Sends crash reports when a crash occurs (including native crash stack traces).
  • Google Analytics 4 Measurement Protocol (direct HTTP POST): Used on Desktop only. Enabled only when configured via environment variables.

Events sent: app_start, session_created, peer_connected, transfer_started, transfer_completed, transfer_cancelled, transfer_failed, text_message_sent / text_message_received, app_end, error

Parameters sent: Platform name, OS version, app version, language setting, number of transferred files, total bytes, transfer duration, transport type (direct P2P / relayed), message length bracket (digit count), error category.

Never Sent
What Telemetry Does Not Include

File names, file contents, message text, peer identifiers, and location data are never sent. Session keys, information related to invite URLs, and any personally identifiable information are never sent either. We also do not collect additional information derived from IP addresses on our own.

Crash Reports
What Crashlytics May Include

Stack traces, device model, OS version, and app version may be included.

How to Opt Out
Turning Telemetry Off

Turn off the "Send telemetry" toggle in the footer at the bottom of the app. On the Web client, the setting is stored in browser storage; on Desktop, it is persisted in the app settings. While telemetry is off, nothing is sent, including Analytics. Crashlytics reports are also not sent for crashes that occur after you turn it off.

When telemetry is enabled, the data described above is sent to Google LLC (Firebase / Google Analytics). See the Google Privacy Policy for details.

Along with enabling telemetry, this policy may be updated together with the services involved (Firebase, etc.). Any significant changes will be announced on this page.

05

No Third-Party Sharing & Analytics

Complete Data Isolation

We do not sell, rent, trade, or share user data with advertising networks, data brokers, analytics providers, or any other commercial third parties. Except when telemetry is enabled, the App sends no user data to any third party (when telemetry is enabled, usage data is sent to Google LLC as described in the previous section).

Because no communication payloads, file data, or personal identifiers are stored on any servers, we cannot provide user data even in response to legal requests or governmental inquiries—there is simply no data to disclose.

06

Compliance & Children's Privacy

Legal & Platform Standards

This policy conforms to Google Play Developer Program Policies, the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI), and global privacy standards.

  • Children's Privacy: The App does not collect personally identifiable information from any user, including children under the age of 13. Telemetry contains no personally identifiable information either. We fully comply with COPPA and similar regulations worldwide.
  • Data Deletion & Access Requests: Because no personal data is retained on servers, formal account deletion or server-side data purging requests are unnecessary. You can remove all locally stored data at any time by deleting saved files or uninstalling the application.
